conclusion: The bounded Fourier ablation fails the confirmed Gaussian smoke: 0 of 24 primary checks pass within 1,000 updates. Its diagnostic continuation also fails: stationary hold 3 of 72, missed shifted reacquisition deadline and shifted hold 1 of 24; frozen control 0 of 48. The final 6,000-update endpoint passes individually (KS 0.0458484), which does not replace the missed acquisition or stability gates. Exactly 6,000 CUDA updates cost 49.887372 adapter-loop seconds. Six exact restores, 219 saved-sample recomputations and two actual-training GIFs validate the published evidence. PR 323 remains the separate negative ablation; its implementation is not adopted.
next_action: Retain Fourier 2 in the ordinary Gaussian architecture. Stop this exact Fourier 0 arm; use the independent shallow diagnostic and separate Tier 1 smoke/Tier 2 stability questions without transferring their gates across architectures. No new training, tuning, seeds or default adoption follows.
